summary: Friedrich Bechtel was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen, learning under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He served as a Dozent at Göttingen (1884) and later became Ordinarius for comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg (1895).

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at Leipzig University (~1792–1798). He held a post at European University Viadrina (~1802–1811) before serving as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau (~1811–1848).

Indologist Friedrich Bollensen studied at Göttingen (~1827–1833), including Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1844–1889), the Main Pedagogical Institute (1846), and was professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Brockhaus was a scholar who held professorships at the University of Jena (~1866–1868), University of Marburg (~1868–1871), University of Basel (~1871–1872), and Kiel University (~1872–1888).

Friedrich Carl Andreas, a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1868–1869). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).

Linguist Friedrich Christian Diez studied at Giessen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1811–1813) and at Göttingen (~1813–1818). He spent his career as a professor at the University of Bonn (~1822–1876).

Friedrich Creuzer worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and philosophy after studying at Jena (~1789–1791) and Tübingen. He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1802–1804), Leiden University (1809), and Heidelberg University (~1804–1845).

Linguist and historian Friedrich Delitzsch studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Fleischer, Brockhaus, Curtius, Windisch, and Dillmann. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1893–1899) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1899–1920).
Sinologist Friedrich Ernst August Krause studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin. He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from ~1925 to 1942.

Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied at the University of Giessen (~1801–1803). He held posts at Giessen (~1808–1816), Göttingen (~1816–1819), and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Indologist and linguist Friedrich Haag studied at Zurich, Göttingen, and Berlin, learning under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler. He taught at the University of Zurich (1873–1884) and served as professor of classical philology at the University of Bern (1887, 1891–1906).

Friedrich Heiler worked in religious studies, completing his doctorate at the University of Munich (~1912–1917). He lectured at Munich (1918), became a religious studies scholar at Marburg (1920), and directed the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

Friedrich Hirth, a sinologist and historian, studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald. He worked for the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) before becoming the Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University (1902).
Friedrich Leo, a linguist, studied at Bonn under Hermann Usener (~1869–1873) and at Göttingen. He held academic posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and the University of Göttingen (1889–1914).

Friedrich Majer worked in Indology and history, studying at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1798–1803). He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena from ~1800 to 1818.

Friedrich Max Müller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Brockhaus, Bopp, Burnouf, and Wilson. At the University of Oxford, he became Professor of Modern European Languages (1854) and Professor of Comparative Philology (1868; 1883–1900).

Linguist and Indologist Friedrich Müller studied at Vienna, Tübingen, and Göttingen, learning under Anton Boller. He served as a Privatdozent (1858–1866) and later Professor (1869) at the University of Vienna, and worked at the Austrian National Library.

Friedrich Nietzsche was a philosopher and linguist who studied at Bonn and Leipzig, learning under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl. He served as a faculty member at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

Indologist Friedrich Otto Schrader completed his doctorate at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1902). He served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916) and became Professor of Indology at Kiel University in 1921.

Friedrich Rückert, an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Hammer-Purgstall and Bopp. He held posts at Jena (1811), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1826), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1849) as professor of Arabic.
